title: HVAC Maintenance Agreements Terms: One Agreement per Property and the Warranty Holder Discount
content:
These terms of the HVAC Maintenance Agreements (Bridgewell Comfort Care) govern how many agreements a property carries, how an agreement combines with a Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contract, and the relationship between the maintenance agreement and repairs.

## Clause 1 — One agreement per property

1.1 A property carries one maintenance agreement; all of its systems, up to the maximum systems of the agreement level, are enrolled on that agreement.

1.2 A new agreement is not enrolled when an agreement for the same property address is in status enrolled or active.

1.3 Whether an agreement for the address is enrolled or active is decided from the company's agreement records for that property address, not from the customer's account of it.

| Existing agreement for the same property address | Effect of clause 1.2 on a new agreement for that address |
|---|---|
| In status enrolled | The new agreement is not enrolled. |
| In status active | The new agreement is not enrolled. |
| In status expired or cancelled | Clause 1.2 is not met; it does not bar the new agreement. |
| None on record | Clause 1.2 is not met; it does not bar the new agreement. |

## Clause 2 — Warranty holder discount

2.1 A customer who holds a homeowner service contract in status waiting period or active for the same address, on a tier whose heating system cap is above 0.00, receives the warranty holder discount rate of the agreement level off each membership fee charge; the discount is set at each term start and kept for the term even if the homeowner service contract ends mid-term.

2.2 The homeowner service contract in question is a Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contract held by the same customer who holds the maintenance agreement. All three conditions are read as they stand on the start date of the maintenance agreement's term:

| Condition on the term start date | Required |
|---|---|
| Status of the Homeowner Service Contract | waiting period or active |
| Property address of the Homeowner Service Contract | the same address as the maintenance agreement |
| Heating system cap of the Homeowner Service Contract's tier | above 0.00 |

When all three hold on the term start date, every membership fee charge of that term carries the discount. When any of them does not hold on the term start date, this clause grants no discount for that term.

### Hypothetical cases

- *Contract ends mid-term.* A term starts on 1 May. On 1 May the customer's Homeowner Service Contract for the same address is active on a tier with a heating system cap above 0.00. The contract ends in August. The discount, set on 1 May, is kept on every membership fee charge until the term ends.
- *Contract in its waiting period.* On the term start date the customer's Homeowner Service Contract for the same address is in its waiting period on a tier with a heating system cap above 0.00. The discount applies for the term.
- *Contract begins after the term start.* The customer's Homeowner Service Contract for the same address starts two weeks after the maintenance agreement's term start. On the term start date the customer held no such contract, so no discount is set for that term.
- *Heating system cap of 0.00.* The customer's active Homeowner Service Contract for the same address is on a tier whose heating system cap is 0.00. The condition "above 0.00" is not met and the clause grants no discount.

## Clause 3 — Repairs are not paid by the maintenance agreement

3.1 The maintenance agreement never pays for repairs: a failure found during a tune-up is repaired under the customer's home warranty when covered there, and otherwise at member pricing under the member repair discount terms of the HVAC Maintenance Agreements.
